events.title: Death of Alexander the Great
events.description: According to many ancient sources and traditional chronologies, Alexander III of Macedon died in Babylon at age 32 after a brief illness, having built an empire stretching from Greece to northwestern India.
events.significance: His death ended the unified Macedonian empire and led to the Wars of the Diadochi, as his generals divided his territories, spreading Hellenistic culture across the Mediterranean and Near East.

events.title: Martin Luther Marries Katharina von Bora
events.description: Protestant reformer Martin Luther married Katharina von Bora, a former nun who had escaped from a convent, in Wittenberg, Germany.
events.significance: The marriage helped establish the model of the Protestant clergy household and symbolized the Reformation's rejection of mandatory clerical celibacy.

events.title: Birth of James Clerk Maxwell
events.description: Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell was born in Edinburgh. He later formulated the classical theory of electromagnetic radiation, unifying electricity, magnetism, and light.
events.significance: Maxwell's equations became a cornerstone of modern physics, paving the way for relativity, quantum theory, and technologies such as radio and radar.

events.title: Miranda v. Arizona Decided
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that criminal suspects must be informed of their right to remain silent and to have an attorney before police interrogation.
events.significance: The decision created the 'Miranda warning' used by U.S. law enforcement and reshaped protections for the rights of the accused.

events.title: Pioneer 10 Crosses the Orbit of Neptune
events.description: NASA's Pioneer 10 spacecraft became the first human-made object to pass beyond the orbit of Neptune, then the outermost planet in its position, on its path out of the solar system.
events.significance: It demonstrated the reach of robotic space exploration and marked a milestone in humanity's journey beyond the planets.
